newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Severn Trent rules out major bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Severn Trent rules out major bid.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Plc is not expecting to bid for another firm on the scale of South West Water, chief executive Vic Cocker told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"No, we are not looking at anything of that sort," he said.
Severn Trent's proposed bid for South West Water was blocked by the government in October, along with one from rival suitor Wessex Water.
A price tag was never set as both predators were waiting for approval before divulging their bid levels.
Severn Trent said in a statement with half-year results that it would now look for growth in waste management, utility related services and water services.
Interim pretax profits totalled 197 million stg, up from 189 million stg and the company paid out a dividend of 10.5 pence, up from 9.2 pence a year ago.
"It is very clear we see our way forward as looking for opportunities" in these areas, Cocker said.
He said the company expected to cultivate these areas primarily through organic growth but that there could be small to medium-sized acquisitions.
The company said in the results statement that it would buy back 10 percent of its shares as soon as was appropriate and Cocker said it would watch markets to decide.
He said plans for further efficiency improvements would be outlined at the final results.
He said the group's waste management company Biffa had turned in "an excellent performance," with profits up nearly 13 percent.

He said Severn Trent aimed for 15-20 percent growth rates in profitability at non-core activities annually, building their contribution up from the current 7.5 percent of profits before interest and tax.
"I hope we are pleasing the market with all the results," he said.
